comment: The two CV inputs do not set the position, they add to it, and they do so on every sample rather than on an edge: src/MentalCartesian.cpp:157 and 165 compute the new position from the current one plus the rounded voltage and store it back, so a steady 1V steps the grid once per sample. That is what the lines for those two jacks say. Both are clamped to 0 and 3 before use, so a negative voltage does nothing. The sixteen buttons are read as levels rather than as edges (line 174), so each one jumps the position to its cell only while it is held; where two are held the higher numbered cell wins, because the loop runs in order. Index order is not panel order for the parameters: the buttons occupy 0 to 15 and the knobs 16 to 31, while the panel puts the knobs on the left and the buttons on the right (lines 269-272). The row outputs sit in a line under the grid, one under each column, and each carries the knob in that column on the current row; the column outputs run down the side, one beside each row, and each carries the knob in that row in the current column. The panel prints Cartesian Sequencer, Left, Right, X CV, X Reset, Up, Down, Y CV, Y reset, Reset, Out, Quant. Out, Column Out and Row Out.
